nodes.name: Rasterize command
nodes.responsibility: Asks the Archboard server for the SVG, then photographs it here and writes the receipt

nodes.name: Rasterizer
nodes.responsibility: Admits one job at a time, starts a browser only when there is work, and retires one that failed a capture
nodes.description: Nothing is started until a job arrives, and the session is stopped with the rasterizer, so no browser outlives the command that needed it. A Chromium that failed one capture is closed rather than trusted with the next.

nodes.name: Bounds and limits
nodes.responsibility: The region, the bitmap size, and the refusal when either is past what may be drawn

nodes.name: Raster session
nodes.responsibility: Draws one SVG at a time in the page it opened: writes the file, loads it, proves the page ready, sets the scale and shoots

nodes.name: Chromium launch
nodes.responsibility: Starts one Chromium, connects to it, opens pages and exact-size windows, and stops it with proof the group and root are gone

nodes.name: DevTools connection
nodes.responsibility: One socket to a target: its calls and events, the page's last complaints, and a Blob streamed into a file

nodes.name: Page readiness
nodes.responsibility: What the page must say before it is photographed, and what the answer must be
nodes.description: The faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job asked for. A bitmap of the wrong size is refused, never cropped.

nodes.name: PNG header
nodes.responsibility: The two numbers from the IHDR of the answered image

nodes.name: Receipt
nodes.responsibility: What was drawn, at what scale, and from which SVG

nodes.name: Chromium
nodes.responsibility: The browser that paints the SVG, runs the recording page and answers over DevTools
nodes.description: Found on this machine, or named by ARCHBOARD_RENDERER_CHROMIUM. Archboard neither ships nor manages it beyond its own child process group.

nodes.name: Headless browser
nodes.responsibility: The one place archboard starts a browser of its own: private, reachable only over loopback DevTools, and proved gone
nodes.description: ADR 0020. The rasterizer and the walkthrough recorder both start their Chromium here, each in its own process group and temporary root; what the pages show is the caller's business.

nodes.name: Chromium executable
nodes.responsibility: Which Chromium to run, spawning it in its own group and temp root, and making that whole group go away

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Draws the SVG, serves the recording page and starts the voice that narrates it

nodes.name: Record command
nodes.responsibility: Picks the walkthrough, has it recorded to the file named, and discards the board afterwards when asked

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Starts the browser a recording needs, opens the page at 1920x1080, and moves the file into place only once that browser has stopped
nodes.description: The browser is started with tab capture accepted without a prompt, audio allowed to play, and a fake microphone playing a second of silence, because voice will not start without a microphone and would hear Chromium's default tone as somebody speaking. An interrupt stops the browser at once, so every call waiting on it fails and nothing is written.

nodes.name: Page driver
nodes.responsibility: Waits until the page is ready, starts it from a user gesture, follows each step and streams the finished file out
nodes.description: Everything the page says crosses as the shared recording state and is parsed as such, so a page from another build is refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.name: Sound conversion
nodes.responsibility: Rewrites an MP4's Opus sound as AAC with ffmpeg, the picture copied, so the file plays with sound in Safari
nodes.description: Chrome on Linux has no AAC encoder, so the page writes MP4 sound as Opus. Without an ffmpeg the file is kept as recorded and the command says what that means.

nodes.name: ffmpeg
nodes.responsibility: Converts the sound and moves the index to the front, so playback starts before the file has arrived
nodes.description: On PATH, or named by ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG.

nodes.name: Recording page
nodes.responsibility: The server's own page on one board: shows the pane alone, paces each step by the voice, and records its tab into one file
nodes.description: The tab capture is picture only. The voice plays through a muted audio element, so nobody hears a recording, and its stream is mixed into the file through one Web Audio destination whose track is there from the first frame. The browser writes the container itself: MP4 with H.264, or WebM with VP9.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: Nobody hears a recording
beats.body: The tab is captured as a picture only, and the voice plays through a muted element. Its stream is mixed into the file through Web Audio instead, on a track that is there from the first frame, because the file cannot take a track that arrives after it started.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the browser has stopped and the sound is converted. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module, each in its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

nodes.name: Recording page

nodes.description: The tab capture is picture only, at Chromium's own 30 frames a second: a rate asked for would also cap the track, which drops frames. Behind the pane a layer nobody sees repaints the whole frame every frame, because Chromium's capture otherwise takes an animation that just stopped for one still running and holds the picture for a quarter of a second. Before it captures its tab, the page draws the subtitle box for two frames, so a GPU has compiled the shaders of its blurred scrim before the first words. The voice plays through a muted audio element, so nobody hears a recording, and its stream is mixed into the file through one Web Audio destination whose track is there from the first frame. The browser writes the container itself: MP4 with H.264, or WebM with VP9.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Runs a recording's two passes: proves ffmpeg first, records the talk in a live page, keeps it, then has it drawn frame by frame
nodes.description: Pass 1's browser is started with audio allowed to play and a fake microphone playing a second of silence, because voice will not start without a microphone and would hear Chromium's default tone as somebody speaking. It captures nothing and needs no GPU: nobody looks at the page, whose reports are what the server hands the voice. The talk is written before pass 2 starts, so a render that fails keeps it. An interrupt stops the browser at once, so every call waiting on it fails and nothing is written.

nodes.name: Page driver
nodes.responsibility: Waits until the page is ready, starts it from a user gesture, follows each step, then streams the voice out and reads the talk's events
nodes.description: Everything the page says crosses as the shared recording state or the talk's log and is parsed as such, so a page from another build is refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.name: ffmpeg
nodes.responsibility: Encodes the frames and the voice into one file: H.264 and AAC in MP4, or VP9 and Opus in WebM, the index at the front
nodes.description: Named by ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, found on PATH, or run through Nix. A recording needs it: without one, the recording is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Recording page
nodes.responsibility: The server's own page on one board: shows the pane alone, paces each step by the voice, and records the talk, never the picture
nodes.description: The voice plays through a muted audio element, so nobody hears a recording, and talk capture taps the same stream. The page hands over the voice as a 16-bit mono 48 kHz WAV and the talk's events by value. It captures no picture: the replay page draws every frame again from the talk.

nodes.name: Replay command
nodes.responsibility: Renders a kept talk to a video again, in either theme, with no voice and no board
nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only to serve the page. A talk that cannot be read, or one of another format version, is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Frame renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a talk frame by frame: opens the replay page in its own Chromium, steps it to each frame's time, captures the frame and hands it to the encoder
nodes.description: One frame is 1/30 s of talk, exactly 1600 samples of the voice, so frame n and sample 1600n are the same moment. Chromium draws in software (--disable-gpu) with its sound muted, and nothing is captured but screenshots. A frame is taken as JPEG at quality 92: the picture is encoded again as 4:2:0 H.264 anyway, and a 2 MP PNG is several times slower to encode and to send. The file moves into place only once ffmpeg has exited and the browser has stopped. A render that fails names the replay command that renders the kept talk again.

nodes.name: Talk files
nodes.responsibility: Writes a talk as talk.json and voice.wav in one atomic rename, and reads one back through the talk's schema
nodes.description: Every recording keeps its talk under the state directory's recordings, where the newest 10 stay. --talk keeps it in a new directory of its own that is never pruned. A talk whose drawn version is not the board's is refused: the board changed while it was recorded, so record again.

nodes.name: Talk capture
nodes.responsibility: Taps the voice through an AudioWorklet and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own 48 kHz clock
nodes.description: The origin is the moment the voice goes live, where the video begins. A stamp is late by at most one audio buffer, about 10 to 21 ms on Linux, which is under one frame. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page
nodes.responsibility: The server's page asked for with ?replay=1: draws a talk's board from the talk alone, one frame at a time on a stepped clock
nodes.description: It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is published and the page has been still for two macrotasks, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. A requestAnimationFrame, an animation left running or a read of another board fails the render and names the frame.

nodes.name: Video encoder
nodes.responsibility: Finds ffmpeg, proves it has the encoders the file needs, and turns the JPEG frames and the voice into that file
nodes.description: ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG comes first, and one named there that does not run is refused by that name, never passed over. Then ffmpeg on PATH, then nix run nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless. With none of them, ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE names both ways to get one. MP4 needs libx264 and aac, and WebM needs libvpx-vp9 and libopus. The frames are converted from full-range BT.601 to BT.709 limited range, and the voice is padded to the last frame.

nodes.name: Nix
nodes.responsibility: Runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless from the machine's registry when no ffmpeg is found
nodes.description: nix run starts the package's own program in its place, so the frame pipe and signals reach ffmpeg itself. The first run fetches the package, which can take minutes.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and a frame is captured only once it is drawn and still. So no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. Anything that moves on real time fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once ffmpeg has exited and the render's browser has stopped. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.
